title: On-device inference for frontier-class models
bottleneck: Running capable models on phones and laptops hits a three-way wall: limited VRAM forces destructive quantization for 70B+ models, memory bandwidth is far below datacenter GPUs, and battery and thermal limits cap sustained compute. Unified memory architectures help capacity but not speed. The result is that personal, private, always-available AI is stuck at small-model capability while frontier intelligence stays in the cloud.
why_it_blocks: Privacy-sensitive, offline, and latency-critical applications can't use cloud models. The on-device gap keeps the most capable AI centralized. Cloud dependence also means latency, cost per query, and data leaving the device - barriers for the most sensitive uses.
current_state: 4-bit 70B-class models run on high-end consumer hardware at reduced speed; frontier-class on-device inference is not close.
